```{python}
#| label: fig-stuck-at
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Limitation of the stuck-at fault model: a CMOS NAND gate with an open defect in the pull-up path of $B$. For $A = 1$, $B = 0$, neither the pull-up nor the pull-down network conducts, so the output floats and keeps its previous value $Y_{n-1}$—a sequential effect that requires two test vectors in the correct order to detect."

import schemdraw as sd
import schemdraw.elements as elm

sd.svgconfig.svg2 = False

with sd.Drawing(canvas='svg') as d:
    d.config(unit=2, fontsize=10)

    # supply rail
    d += elm.Vdd().at((2, 8.2)).label('$V_\\mathrm{DD}$')
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((2, 8.2), (2, 7.6))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0.5, 7.6), (4.5, 7.6))
    d += elm.Dot().at((2, 7.6))

    # PMOS 1 (A), mirrored so the gate faces input A
    p1 = elm.PFet(bulk=False).at((0.5, 7.6)).anchor('source').theta(180).flip()
    d += p1
    d += elm.Label().at((0.9, p1.gate[1])).label('$M_{P1}$', halign='left')
    # PMOS 2 (B) with open defect at its drain
    p2 = elm.PFet(bulk=False).at((4.5, 7.6)).anchor('source').theta(0)
    d += p2
    d += elm.Label().at((4.1, p2.gate[1])).label('$M_{P2}$', halign='right')

    # output node
    d += elm.Line().at(p1.drain).to((0.5, 4.5))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0.5, 4.5), (4.5, 4.5))
    d += elm.Dot().at((2, 4.5))
    # open defect in the branch of MP2
    d += elm.Line().at(p2.drain).to((4.5, 5.6))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((4.5, 5.0), (4.5, 4.5))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((4.35, 5.45), (4.65, 5.15)).color('red')
    d += elm.Label().at((4.1, 5.3)).label('open', color='red',
                                           halign='right')

    # NMOS stack, MN1 mirrored so the gate faces input A
    n1 = elm.NFet(bulk=False).at((2, 4.5)).anchor('drain').theta(180).flip()
    d += n1
    d += elm.Label().at((2.4, n1.gate[1])).label('$M_{N1}$', halign='left')
    n2 = elm.NFet(bulk=False).at(n1.source).anchor('drain').theta(0)
    d += n2
    d += elm.Label().at((1.6, n2.gate[1])).label('$M_{N2}$', halign='right')
    d += elm.Ground().at(n2.source)

    # input A
    xa, ya = -1.6, (p1.gate[1] + n1.gate[1]) / 2
    d += elm.Line().at(p1.gate).to((xa, p1.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().at(n1.gate).to((xa, n1.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((xa, p1.gate[1]), (xa, n1.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((xa, ya), (xa - 0.8, ya))
    d += elm.Dot().at((xa, ya))
    d += elm.Dot(open=True).at((xa - 0.8, ya)).label('$A$', 'left')

    # input B
    xb, yb = 7.4, n2.gate[1] + 1.0
    d += elm.Line().at(p2.gate).to((xb, p2.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().at(n2.gate).to((xb, n2.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((xb, p2.gate[1]), (xb, n2.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((xb, yb), (xb + 0.8, yb))
    d += elm.Dot().at((xb, yb))
    d += elm.Dot(open=True).at((xb + 0.8, yb)).label('$B$', 'right')

    # output Y
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((4.5, 4.5), (6.2, 4.5))
    d += elm.Dot().at((4.5, 4.5))
    d += elm.Dot(open=True).at((6.2, 4.5)).label('$Y$', 'top')
```
